attempts.label: DANDI:001285
attempts.paper_title: Electroencephalogram signatures of loss and recovery of consciousness from propofol
attempts.entry_title: EEG signatures of loss and recovery of consciousness from propofol (Purdon et al. 2013)
attempts.summary: None of the paper's main findings could be tested in this data, because the dandiset holds the EEG of one of the ten volunteers and none of the task data. The loss of response to clicks before verbal stimuli, the timing of unconsciousness, the beta and gamma rise before it, the frontal alpha mode and the phase-amplitude shift all need the button-press responses, which are not deposited. The 64 channels also lack names and positions, so spatial results cannot be built. All 22 claims were blocked, and none reproduced or failed. The one subject's band-power course tests no claim.
attempts.description: Checks dandiset 001285 against the findings of Purdon et al. (2013) on behaviour and EEG during gradual propofol induction and emergence in 10 volunteers. The dandiset holds the 64-channel EEG of one subject, without channel names, behavioural responses, infusion levels or time markers, so none of the paper's 22 claims can be tested; the notebook describes the file and checks it against its description.

outcomes.notes: Needs each subject's time series of responses to the click and verbal stimuli. The NWB file holds no stimuli, button presses, trials, events or intervals, and the dandiset holds 1 of the 10 subjects. Searched the file (every group), the dandiset's assets (one file), and DANDI for other dandisets of the study (001286 and 001287 carry the same description and hold no files).

EON and LOC are defined from the response-probability curves, and the responses are not in the dandiset (see fig1c-clicks-lost-before-verbal). The file holds no time markers either, and only 1 of 10 subjects, so the across-subject median and quartiles cannot be formed.
The group curves pool the responses of 10 subjects aligned at LOC; no responses are deposited and 9 of 10 subjects are absent.
As fig1e-group-induction, aligned at ROC.
EOFF is defined from Pclicks, which needs the responses to the click stimuli, not in the dandiset; the count is over 10 subjects, of which 1 is deposited.
ROC and EOFF come from the responses, not in the dandiset; 1 of 10 subjects.

The spectrogram is aligned at LOC, which the paper derives from the behavioural responses (not deposited), and significance is a sign test across 10 subjects (1 deposited). The channel near Fz and the Laplacian also cannot be formed, as the 64 channels have no names or positions (metadata_insufficient). In the deposited subject, beta power (median over the 64 unnamed channels) steps to about 2 times the first 15 min of the file at minute 17 and to 5.5 to 9.9 times (median 7.6 over minutes 33 to 47) at minute 33, which describes the file and tests nothing.
Needs LOC (from the responses, not deposited) and the sign test across 10 subjects (1 deposited); the channel near Fz cannot be identified (no channel names or positions; metadata_insufficient).

Needs LOC (not deposited) and the median map across 10 subjects (1 deposited). The channel groups (frontal, temporal, parietal, occipital) also cannot be formed, as the channels have no names or positions (metadata_insufficient).
Needs ROC and EOFF (from the responses, not deposited) and the sign test across 10 subjects (1 deposited); no channel names for Fz (metadata_insufficient).

The claim's quantity is the group median across 10 subjects of low-frequency power in the unconscious state (between LOC and ROC, or at LOC + 15 min) over baseline, at the channel near Fz or over channels. LOC and ROC are not deposited, 9 of 10 subjects are absent, and the channels have no names (metadata_insufficient). As a description of the file only, low-frequency power, median over the 64 unnamed channels without a Laplacian, is 6.5 to 34 times its level in the first 15 min from minute 49 to minute 97 (median 15.4 over minutes 60 to 100; 16.3 over the 55 channels with SDs below 300 uV). The reference period was chosen after looking at the data, and the period is not shown to be the unconscious state, so this is no evidence for the claim.

Needs the group spectrogram aligned at LOC, with the start of the transition at EON or 30 min before LOC; LOC and EON come from the responses, not deposited, and 9 of 10 subjects are absent. No channel names for Fz (metadata_insufficient).
As fig3a-induction-traveling-peak, aligned at ROC with EOFF; neither is deposited.

Needs all seven behavioural time points (from the responses, not deposited), the group median across 10 subjects (1 deposited), and channel groups, which cannot be formed without channel names or positions (metadata_insufficient).
As fig3b-frontal-median-frequency-power; the frontal and occipital groups cannot be formed either.

The timing part needs LOC and ROC (not deposited) and the group mean over 10 subjects (1 deposited). The spatial part, whether the baseline mode is occipital, needs channel positions or names, which the file does not hold (metadata_insufficient); the full baseline period is not marked either.

The unconscious cross-spectral matrix is taken from LOC to ROC (not deposited); group over 10 subjects (1 deposited); frontal channels cannot be identified (no names or positions; metadata_insufficient).

The paper's test uses the unconscious mode between LOC and ROC and the group mean over 10 subjects; LOC and ROC are not deposited and 9 of 10 subjects are absent. The test is that of fig4cd-frontal-alpha-mode, defined as fig4ab-occipital-alpha-mode, which applies the Laplacian (the paper applies it to "this and subsequent analyses"); the Laplacian needs channel names or positions, which the file does not hold (metadata_insufficient).

The epochs are placed relative to LOC (not deposited) and the count is over 10 subjects (1 deposited); the frontal channel near Fz and its Laplacian cannot be formed without channel names or positions (metadata_insufficient).
As fig5-trough-max-induction, 10 to 40 min after LOC.
As fig5-trough-max-induction, aligned at ROC (not deposited).
The epochs are centred at LOC and LOC + 30 min (LOC not deposited) and averaged across 10 subjects (1 deposited); no channel names for Fz (metadata_insufficient).

findings.statement: The dandiset holds one subject (sub-Subject001), where the paper and the dandiset's own description report ten volunteers. Dandisets 001286 and 001287 carry the same description of the study and hold no files. Searching DANDI for propofol, Purdon, Yousefi, anesthesia, consciousness, Emery Brown and EEG found no other dandiset with these data.

The behavioural task is not deposited (stimulus times and types, button presses), nor the infusion levels and their times, nor the behavioural markers EON, LOC, ROC and EOFF. Every finding of the paper is defined from or aligned to these, so none can be tested.

The 64 EEG channels have no names, positions or bad-channel marks; the file has no electrode table, although the paper digitized each subject's electrode positions. The frontal channel the paper analyses, the Laplacian reference and every spatial result need them. Nine channels have SDs above 300 uV, which suggests noisy channels the paper would have excluded.

The EEG is stored as a generic TimeSeries (named example_timeseries, description "no description") with data of shape 64 x 2,316,950, channels first. NWB puts time on the first axis, so pynwb reports 64 samples. The series is not an ElectricalSeries and has no electrodes.

The subject's age is P30D (30 days) for a volunteer the paper describes as 18 to 36 years old. The session start time (2025-01-10T14:24:38Z) equals the file creation date, the date of the conversion, not of the recording. The identifier (NWB123) and session description (EEG Session Example) are placeholders, and the ORCID in the file's notes (0000-0001-2345-6789) differs from the contact's ORCID on DANDI (0009-0006-8777-8262).
Subject001 is not linked to the paper's numbering of its ten subjects (for example subject 7, shown in Figure 1), so the deposited recording cannot be matched to any per-subject result of the paper.

The values are consistent with the description where they can be checked. The 60 Hz mains peak and the roll-off above 100 Hz fit the stated 250 Hz rate, the amplitudes fit microvolts, no channel duplicates another, there are no gaps, and the band-power time course (beta rising at minutes 17 and 33, low-frequency and alpha power high from minute 48 to minute 97) has the outline of a gradual propofol induction and emergence, against a reference period (minutes 0 to 15) chosen after looking at the data. The duration does not match. The described protocol (a 20-min baseline, ten 14-min levels and 20 min after the infusion) implies about 180 min, and the file holds 154.5 min; the file marks none of the protocol's phases, so which part is shorter or missing cannot be told.
